title: A token you can say aloud
subtitle: river-cloud-3847 is the whole key: Maya says it on a call, Hugo types it, Eve hears it a week too late. 8 panels.
rule: Every line a character says is the storyboard's, not a quote, and is marked not_a_quote; evidence panels quote this site's pages word for word, which the build checks.

scenes.title: A token you can say aloud
scenes.subtitle: Two words and four digits. Then let it expire.
scenes.note: The friendly token: one short string that is the whole credential for one transfer.

scenes.caption: On the phone

cast.says: It's three words, Hugo. river, cloud, three eight four seven.

scenes.note: The moment a friendly token is for: two people, one call, no screen to scan.

scenes.caption: Two words and four digits
scenes.note: The word list is send.sgraph.ai's own, so a token made on either site opens on the other.

scenes.caption: Both sides derive the same two things
scenes.note: The transfer id and the key both come from the token, in both browsers; the server maps nothing.

scenes.caption: Hugo types it

cast.says: river… cloud… three eight four seven.

scenes.note: The open page accepts a token typed in, or the link that carries it.

scenes.caption: Eve was listening

cast.says: I heard it. A week later.

scenes.note: A token can be guessed offline by anyone holding the ciphertext, so it suits a link that expires. This one did.

scenes.caption: What a friendly token is for

evidence.quote: a friendly token is for a link that expires, a file that is not worth that effort, and a moment when speaking it is the point; a random key is for everything else.

scenes.note: Quoted from the QR codes page, word for word.

scenes.punchline: Say it, type it, scan it. Then let it expire.
scenes.note: The trade, stated on the send page where the choice is made.
